properties.description:
tools/run_ci_gates.py already reads the gate list from ci.yml through skill_lint's parser and already knows each gate's command, exit code and elapsed time; today it prints them and discards them. This capability writes that same material out as a machine-readable file — one row per gate with name, command, exit code, duration, plus the commit sha and timestamp for the run as a whole — and CI publishes it as a build artifact.

The runner's three existing refusals carry over and are the reason this is cheap: running zero gates is already a failure rather than a pass, a near-empty parse of the workflow is already refused as broken, and a failing gate already fails the EXIT CODE and not only the printed summary. A run record inherits those, so a record showing nothing ran is distinguishable from a record showing nothing failed.

Deliberately stops at the file. Nothing maps gate names to Verification ids and nothing writes a status; that is the open half.

WHY THIS IS NOT cap:the-gate-list-is-run-not-only-cross-checked, which lives in the same script: that capability is EXECUTION — the gate list can be run locally in one command, read from the workflow rather than restated — and it is already realized. This one is EVIDENCE — the run leaves something behind that outlives the terminal — and it is unbuilt. Folding the second into the first would have made a realized capability assert that unbuilt work is done, which is the one thing the status field must never be able to say by accident.
properties.name: The gate runner emits a run record — every gate it ran, its exit code, its duration, and the commit
